text:
Aditi: quick heads-up — ran a weekend sim targeting EU edge (egress cap 4Gbps/node) with current mix: 70% hosted, 20% dedicated, 10% preemptible. seeing a fattening tail in tokens/sec and queue depth around shoulder hours. results pasted below.

Marco: can you drop the numbers?

Aditi: yes — short paste: ```sim: weekend-eu-edge-2026 --seed=42 --traffic-mix=prod-weekend
summary:
  p50_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu: 42k
  p90_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu: 61k
  avg_concurrent_requests_per_gpu: 28
  p95_request_queue_ms: 260
  preemptions_hours_lost: 38
  observed_egress_util_peak: 3.6Gbps
  cost_delta_vs-baseline: +18% (higher retries + preempt overhead)
notes: tail is driven by small fraction (~3%) of long seq requests + egress throttling-induced slowdowns causing KV cache misses.```

Jules: hmm egress cap hitting 90%+ on a few nodes? which AZs showed that?

Aditi: mostly eu-west-1a and 1c (FR & IE hosts). Also the preemptible churn amplifies cache warmups — when a preempted task moves, downstream request sees KV miss and adds ~120-250ms per request => cascades.

Rana: +18% weekend cost is painful. any mitigations that don't need heavy infra purchases?

Aditi: short list of experiments with estimated impact and owners: 
- egress-aware routing (route long-seq to FR hosts with spare egress) — est cost impact: -3% and p95 queue -70ms (owner: Marco)
- prefix TTL bump from 3s -> 15s for small prefixes (reduces KV churn) — est cost impact: -4% and p95 queue -90ms (owner: Jules)
- preemptible smoothing (limit evictions from same rack) — est cost impact: -2% and reduces lost hours by ~10 (owner: infra-ops)
- adaptive batch caps for long sequences (cap tokens/batch when egress throttling detected) — est cost impact: -1.5% (owner: Aditi)

Marco: egress-aware routing sounds reasonable. how invasive? any perf regressions for short seqs?

Aditi: low invasiveness — routing policy pick based on SLO hints + egress headroom probe; short seqs stay on default fast path. fallback exists. added config prototype: ```routing:
  egress_probe_interval_s: 10
  egress_threshold_ratio: 0.85
  prefer_hosts_with_egress_free: true
  qualify_for_routing: request.long_seq == true || request.predicted_tokens > 1024
```

infra-ops: we can land routing rule in ~2 days as a feature flag. will need a quick canary (10% traffic FR only) and rollback hook.

Jules: prefix TTL increase — any risk of staleness? these are only small prefixes for KV metadata, not model params. safe to 15s for weekend trial.

Rana: if combined mitigations hit your estimates, net weekend cost change is ~ -1% and SLOs improve — that's acceptable. finance ok with small trials.

Marco: rollback criteria? what metrics to watch during canary?

Aditi: proposal: revert if any of: p95_queue_ms increases > 30% vs baseline for 5m window, error rate uptick > 0.1%, or tokens/sec throughput drop > 6% sustained for 10m. also watch egress_util by AZ.

infra-bot: deploy plan created: deploy/egress-aware-routing/flag-2026-03
 - canary: FR AZ only 10% traffic
 - monitor: p95_queue_ms, error_rate, egress_util_AZ
 - auto-rollback triggers: based on thresholds from Aditi

Aditi: ok owners: Marco -> route flag + canary, Jules -> prefix TTL change + small perf check, infra-ops -> preemptible smoothing config, I'll wire adaptive batch cap and observability.

Jules: ping me when you have perf probe, I'll run synthetic long-seq workload.

Marco: I'll own the rollout and dashboards — will schedule canary tomorrow morning at low-traffic window.

Rana: finance will keep monitoring cost trends, please tag me in the canary report.

Aditi: thanks. labeling action items in the ticket: #infra-1802. will update with raw sim logs and a short doc on how egress probes work. :thumbsup:
